author: eskultety
body:
This is primarily motivated by the fact that currently there's no straight forward way of debugging our production code whilst running integration tests on it simply due to the fact that we're running our integration tests in a containerized environment and so a mere `pytest -s` would not be propagated properly as it would be the case if we tested in local environments with simply the `hermeto` package installed.

This is not to say that one currently cannot debug our tests, but that involves a few manual steps first:
- clone the integration-tests git repo
- checkout the correct branch (depending on the pytest ID)
- create a Python virtual environment and install the current development version of hermeto inside with the `-e` flag (i.e. development version)
- add your `breakpoint()` to the hermeto production code
- run `hermeto <cmd> on the checked out branch of the integration-tests repo`

When one understands what needs to be done, it's not that bad and is also fast because one runs locally instead of inside a containerized environment, however, that's no fun for infrequent (drive-by) contributors. It really needs to be as simple as "setting a breakpoint & done". Let me introduce a new testing image & logic that comes with Python debuggers [ipdb, pudb] pre-installed and does exactly ^that! This testing image is ONLY ever used when debugging is enabled, so our defaults when it comes to testing are not changed in any way.

This is how you can try this (with a breakpoint set somewhere in the production code):
```shell
pytest -s --debug-hermeto -k '<test_filter>' test/integration
OR
nox -s all-integration-tests -- -s --debug-hermeto -k '<test_filter>`
```
^that should give you an interactive `ipdb` session (the default). If you want something more interactive, then you can set
`HERMETO_TEST_DEBUGGER=pudb` which will use PuDB instead of ipdb.

Now, onto the test image. The test image is based on [toolbox](https://github.com/containers/toolbox). That's not a requirement for a test image, but a deliberate decision on giving the test image a second purpose - a complete interactive development environment to work with Hermeto! You don't need to install all Hermeto's dependencies (cargo, npm, yarn, etc.) to your local development machine (you can feel the pain even more if you use an immutable distro), you get them in the image which is functionally the same image as our production image. What you get on top is:

- mounted your $HOME automatically by toolbox
- ability to execute `podman` and `buildah` from within a nested containerized environment which is otherwise not possible/very problematic
- dbus access
- & more

Follow the docs on how to create a toolbox container, but TL;DR:
```shell
# inside our git repo with this PR checked out
$ podman build -t hermeto-toolbox -f toolbox/Containerfile.toolbox
$ toolbox create -i hermeto-toolbox:latest hermeto-toolbox
$ toolbox enter hermeto-toolbox
```

author: rshade
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: vaibhav541
body:
## Problem
The pod is experiencing high CPU usage and frequent restarts due to an unoptimized graph processing algorithm in the cpu_intensive_task() function. The current implementation creates unnecessarily large graphs (20 nodes) and runs the algorithm continuously without any rate limiting or resource constraints.

## Changes
- Reduced graph size from 20 to 10 nodes to decrease computational complexity
- Added 0.5s sleep between iterations for rate limiting
- Added timeout break if an iteration takes more than 2 seconds
- Reduced max_depth parameter in path finding from 10 to 5

## Testing
- Verified CPU usage stays within acceptable limits
- Confirmed core functionality remains intact
- Tested pod stability over extended period

## Impact
This change will significantly reduce CPU usage and prevent pod restarts while maintaining the essential functionality of the graph processing algorithm.

## Title
refactor: remove month/year fields from CurrentUpdate after switching to scheduled publishing

## Purpose
- Previously, `CurrentUpdate` relied on `month` and `year` fields for validation and typing.
- After migrating server logic to scheduled publishing, these fields became redundant.
- To align with the new publishing flow, the related validation checks and type definitions were removed.

## Changes  
- Simplified validation logic by removing `month` and `year` field checks (`currentUpdateStore.ts`)
- Removed `month` and `year` fields from `CurrentUpdate` type(`public.ts`)

author: ruaridhmacd
body:
## Description

**I've resolved the sub-commodities issue, so I've moved this to a full PR**

### Gurobi

Gurobi (via Gurobi.jl) is currently a requirement to run Macro. That creates problems for users who do not have a Gurobi license, including GitHub automated workflows. In particular, this prevents MacroEnergy.jl being registered in the Julia package registry. However, we would like to include Gurobi-specific instructions as part of Macro

To resolve this, I’ve tested moving the Gurobi-specific functions to an extension: MacroEnergyGurobiExt.jl. This is part of the MacroEnergy.jl repo, under `/ext/ MacroEnergyGurobiExt.jl`

Gurobi.jl becomes a “weak dependency” instead of a required dependency. It will only be loaded if Gurobi.jl is in the user’s project environment, i.e.:

- `using MacroEnergy`  loads regular MacroEnergy.jl code
- `Pkg.add(“Gurobi”` or `using Gurobi` loads Gurobi.jl and MacroEnergyGurobiExt.jl

To call or create a Gurobi Environment, we call `opt_env(:Gurobi)` or `opt_env(Gurobi.Optimizer)`. This will return a Gurobi Environment for each worker. 

This is extensible to other optimizers and will return nothing if not needed,  e.g. `opt_env(:HiGHS)` or `opt_env(HiGHS.Optimizer)` both return `nothing`.

I chose to use `nothing` instead of `missing` as the documentation I read suggests `missing` is more intended for numerical data instead of Julia objects.

--- 

### Sub-commodities and other user-generated additions

One side-affect of moving the Gurobi instructions (and any subsequent code which relies on a license or difficult to access package) is that MacroEnergy may precompile multiple times. I found that this ran into issues with our use of `include` calls as part of the `__init__` function and in other places.

After experimenting with a couple solutions, I found that the most robust is to move all user-provided additions to their own module which is part of the example directory. This has a few benefits:

1. The user additions are back to being in the example directory as opposed to the MacroEnergy repo files, which will not work for users downloading MacroEnergy as a package, not repository.
2. Users can add commodities, sub-commodities, assets, or any other additions using their own Module.

As it's currently set up, the module is loaded as part of the `run_case` function. MacroEnergy will create a `tmp` folder in the users example folder, create the module and include any commodities, sub-commodities, and assets it finds.

body:
Hey! First of all, really thanks for using **Poku** (#2181) 🐷✨

I've made some small adjustments to the tests to make sure they all run properly 🙋🏻‍♂️

---

Currently, these tests are being completely ignored due to manual inclusion in _.pokurc.jsonc_:

- _lib/helpers/envcontext.poku.js_
- _lib/managers/docker.poku.js_

Instead, I just updated it to `"include": ["lib"]`, allowing dynamic searching from `.poku.js` filter.

---

By ensuring that the two tests mentioned were performed, they were pointing out some failures for specific behaviors of **Windows** and **macOS**:

- **Windows**
  - **Java** and **Swift** are not available in the CI.
- **macOS**
  - **Go** is not available in the CI.
- For both **Windows** and **macOS**, **Docker** is not available in the CI.

---

Unlike other test runners for **JavaScript**, [**Poku** preserves the `async/await` behavior for tests in `describe`, `it`, and `test` methods](https://poku.io/docs/philosophy#javascript-essence-for-tests-).

---

- I also adjusted some non-existent method calls in the **nvm** tests.
- By actually running all the tests, I noticed that unlimited concurrency was causing **Node.js** version 20 to crash on **macOS**. I just kept the default behavior that dynamically checks for the available parallelism/cpu number.

---

Please feel free to ask and review these changes in the tests 🤝

> [!NOTE]
>
> About #2176, I didn't look into it too deeply, but the `FATAL ERROR: invalid array length Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory` error seems to be related to the extensive number of _symlinks_ found when a test runner is searching for tests in directories recursively (more specifically, in the `"/"` directory).

author: arturaz
body:
When invoking `semanticDbData` on a module with dependencies, those dependencies are compiled using `compile`.

Which means that if you do `__.semanticDbData`, we could get away by just using `semanticDbData` for the module dependencies, but instead run `compile` for all of them and then run another compilation via `semanticDbData`, effectively doing twice the work.

This PR eliminates the need for `compile`.

Tested manually on gatling codebase, this cuts down `__.semanticDbData` time from 50s to 30s.

---

Fixes https://github.com/com-lihaoyi/mill/issues/5717

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements 35 specific parameter classes for the Balancing group in the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform API, following the established pattern from Load and Generation groups.

## Overview

All classes inherit from `BalancingParams` and provide preset values for specific ENTSO-E Balancing endpoints. Each class encapsulates the required document types, process types, and business types for their respective endpoints while allowing users to configure domains, time periods, and other parameters.

## Implementation Details

**Files Added:**
- `src/entsoe_api_py/Balancing/specific_params.py` - Contains all 35 parameter classes
- `src/entsoe_api_py/Balancing/__init__.py` - Module exports and imports  
- `test_balancing_params.py` - Comprehensive test suite covering all classes

**Classes Implemented by Category:**

**Core Balancing Endpoints (17.1.x series - 8 classes):**
- Cross Border Balancing, Accepted Aggregated Offers, Activated Balancing Energy, Prices of Activated Balancing Energy, Volumes and Prices of Contracted Reserves, Imbalance Prices, Total Imbalance Volumes, Financial Expenses and Income for Balancing

**Balancing Energy Bids (12.3.x series - 6 classes):**
- Balancing Energy Bids, Balancing Energy Bids Archives, Aggregated Balancing Energy Bids, Procured Balancing Capacity, Allocation and Use of Cross-zonal Balancing Capacity, Current Balancing State

**Reserve Capacity Management (187.x/188.x/189.x/190.x series - 14 classes):**
- FCR Total Capacity, Shares of FCR Capacity (including legacy), FRR & RR Capacity Outlook, FRR and RR Actual Capacity (including legacy), Sharing arrangements between areas, Exchanged Reserve Capacity

**Interface Functions (IF series - 7 classes):**
- Cross Border Marginal Prices for aFRR, Netted and Exchanged Volumes, Elastic Demands, Changes to Bid Availability, Border Capacity Limitations, HVDC Line Constraints, Criteria Application Process Results

## Usage Example

```python
from entsoe_api_py.Balancing import ImbalancePricesParams, CrossBorderBalancingParams

# Get imbalance prices for a specific bidding zone
imbalance_params = ImbalancePricesParams(
    security_token="your_token_here",
    period_start=202308152200,
    period_end=202308162200,
    bidding_zone_domain="10YBE----------2"  # Belgium
)

# Get cross-border balancing data between two areas
cross_border_params = CrossBorderBalancingParams(
    security_token="your_token_here", 
    period_start=202308152200,
    period_end=202308162200,
    acquiring_domain="10YBE----------2",  # Belgium
    connecting_domain="10YFR-RTE------C"  # France
)
```

## Key Features

- **Consistent Architecture**: All classes follow the same inheritance pattern and parameter structure as existing Load and Generation classes
- **Comprehensive Documentation**: Each class includes detailed docstrings with links to ENTSO-E transparency platform data views
- **Type Safety**: Full type hints for better IDE support and error prevention
- **Thorough Testing**: 35/35 classes tested with comprehensive validation of inheritance, parameters, and functionality

## Validation

The implementation has been thoroughly tested:
- ✅ All 35 classes instantiate correctly with proper inheritance from `BalancingParams`
- ✅ All required parameters are accessible via the `params` dictionary
- ✅ Each class has unique codes and appropriate document types
- ✅ Code compiles without syntax errors and imports work correctly
- ✅ Maintains consistency with existing codebase patterns

This completes the implementation of Balancing parameter classes as requested, providing developers with easy access to all major ENTSO-E Balancing endpoints through a consistent, well-documented API.

#### **Changes Overview**
This PR introduces several significant updates to the editor functionality and UI:

1. **Converted `useEditor` from TipTap to Custom BlockNoteSchema**  
   - Replaced the existing TipTap-based editor with a custom BlockNoteSchema implementation.  
   - **Why?** BlockNoteSchema provides more out-of-the-box features, is easier to maintain, and is more scalable for future enhancements.  
   - **Note:** This change was inspired by the open-source project [Mintter](https://github.com/seed-hypermedia/mintter). Huge thanks to their team for the guidance and examples!

2. **Added Theme Switching in Bottom Left Corner Using Tamagui**  
   - Implemented a theme switcher in the bottom-left corner of the editor interface.  
   - Utilized Tamagui for a seamless and responsive UI experience.  
   - **Why?** This improves user customization and aligns with modern design practices.

3. **Added Image and Video Support**  
   - Enabled image and video embedding in the editor.  
   - **Why?** This enhances the editor's functionality, making it more versatile for content creation.  
   - **Note:** The current implementation needs further optimization for performance and usability. This will be addressed in future updates.

---

#### **Why This PR is a Single Unit**
I understand that these changes could have been broken into smaller, more focused PRs. However, many of these updates were interdependent and built on top of each other, making it challenging to separate them without causing inconsistencies or breaking functionality. This PR serves as a comprehensive update for testing and gathering feedback.

---

#### **Next Steps**
- **Error Fixing and Import Cleanup:** There are several errors and import changes that need to be addressed. These will be resolved after merging, as this PR is primarily for temporary testing and gathering opinions.  
- **Optimization:** Image and video support will be further optimized in subsequent updates.  
- **Feedback Welcome:** Please share your thoughts on the changes, especially the BlockNoteSchema implementation and theme switcher. Your feedback will help refine these features before finalizing them.

---

#### **Acknowledgments**
Special thanks to the [Mintter](https://github.com/seed-hypermedia/mintter) open-source project for their work on BlockNoteSchema, which greatly influenced this implementation. Their contributions to the community are invaluable!

author: falkoschindler
body:
### Motivation

NiceGUI 3.0 should upgrade its Tailwind dependency to version 4 which has been released quite a while ago.

### Implementation

This PR had to address several challenges:

- update package.json and extract_core_libraries to use Tailwind from node_modules/ instead of http://cdn.tailwindcss.com/
- remove warning about not using this version in production
- introduce CSS layers to properly integrate Tailwind with Quasar and NiceGUI's CSS rules
- update our hack to preserve borders of card children
- fix a conflict between Tailwind's "inline" class a Quasar components like QSelect, QCheckbox and QRadio
- update documentation and tests to use new border classes
- update links in documentation
- ~~update~~ remove the `.tailwind` API

An open question is what to do with the `.tailwind` API: It is getting more and more useless after Tailwind removed classes like "p-0" and mainly kept generic classes like "p-<number>", "p-(<custom-property>)", and "p-[<value>]". We could try to improve the API to support numbers beside literal strings, but it would require significant work. Apart from that the current PR causes several breaking changes because, e.g., [borders](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/border-style) now can start with "border-" _or_ "divide-". Therefore the literal string options change from "solid" etc. to "border-solid", "divide-solid" etc. It feels like Tailwind is getting to complex and flexible to keep trying to mirror its API. A potential way forward could be to release the new API as deprecated and discourage using it until we shut it down in NiceGUI 4.0.

- [x] The implementation is complete.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements the highwater mark update functionality for the cluster client and service with a simplified interface that takes only the highwater mark parameter, plus the ability to register a channel to receive highwater mark updates.

## Changes Made

### Protocol Definitions
- Added `HighwaterMarkUpdateRequest` message with `node_id` (string) and `highwater_mark` (uint64) fields
- Added `HighwaterMarkUpdateResponse` message with `error` (string) field
- Added `COMMAND_TYPE_HIGHWATER_MARK_UPDATE` to the Command enum
- Regenerated proto files using protoc

### Client Implementation
Added the `BroadcastHWM` method on the cluster client with the signature:

```go
func (c *Client) BroadcastHWM(hwm uint64, retries int, timeout time.Duration, nodeAddr ...string) (map[string]*proto.BroadcastResponse, error)
```

The implementation:
- Returns a map where keys are node addresses and values are highwater mark update responses
- Sends highwater mark updates to all specified nodes in parallel using goroutines
- Handles retries for failed requests
- Waits for all responses or timeout (whichever comes first)
- Properly handles connection pooling and error handling following existing patterns
- Automatically uses the client's local node address for the `node_id` field in the request
- Creates the `HighwaterMarkUpdateRequest` proto internally from the provided highwater mark parameter

### Service Implementation
- Added highwater mark update request statistics counter (`numBroadcastHWMRequest`)
- Added `numHWMUpdateDropped` statistics counter for tracking dropped updates when the registered channel is full
- Added handler case for `COMMAND_TYPE_HIGHWATER_MARK_UPDATE` in the service
- The handler responds with no error and follows the same pattern as other command handlers
- Added `RegisterHWMUpdate` method to allow registration of a channel for receiving highwater mark updates
- The method signature takes `chan<- uint64` to send only the highwater mark value (not the full request structure)
- Modified handler to send updates to registered channel if available using non-blocking sends
- Added statistics tracking for dropped updates when the registered channel is full

### Testing
Added comprehensive tests covering:
- Single node updates
- Multiple node updates 
- Empty node list handling
- Error response handling
- Service-side request handling
- Channel registration and receiving updates with the new uint64 signature

All existing tests continue to pass, ensuring no regression in functionality.

## Example Usage

```go
client := cluster.NewClient(dialer, timeout)
client.SetLocal("node-1", nil)  // Set local node information
responses, err := client.BroadcastHWM(12345, 3, time.Second*5, "node1:8080", "node2:8080")
// responses is now a map[string]*proto.HighwaterMarkUpdateResponse where keys are node addresses

// Register for highwater mark updates
hwmCh := make(chan uint64, 10)
service.RegisterHWMUpdate(hwmCh)
// hwmCh will now receive uint64 highwater mark values when they arrive
```

Fixes #2230.

author: fauziakram
body:
**Refine Mobility Evaluation for Better Positional Understanding**

This pull request introduces a significant refinement to our engine's evaluation function by improving how piece mobility is calculated. The goal is to give the engine a more nuanced and realistic understanding of piece activity, which should translate to stronger positional play.

---

### Motivation

Previously, our mobility score was calculated based on the total number of squares a piece could move to, as long as those squares weren't occupied by friendly pieces. While a good first-order approximation, this approach has a flaw: it treats a move to a safe, open square the same as a move to a square directly controlled by an opponent's pawn. In reality, the latter is often a blunder, not a useful option.

This change corrects that by teaching the engine to value *safe* mobility over raw mobility.

---

### Description of Changes

1.  **Introduction of Safe Mobility Area:**
    *   Within the `evaluate()` function, before the main piece loop begins, we now calculate a `safe_mobility_area` for each color.
    *   This bitmask represents all squares on the board that are **not** occupied by friendly pieces and are **not** attacked by enemy pawns.

2.  **Updated Mobility Calculation:**
    *   The mobility score for Knights, Bishops, Rooks, and Queens is now calculated based on the number of attack squares that intersect with this new `safe_mobility_area`.
    *   This ensures the engine rewards pieces that have access to secure and useful squares, rather than just a high number of moves, many of which may be tactically unsound.

3.  **Re-tuned Mobility Parameters:**
    *   Since the new calculation method naturally results in lower average mobility counts, the per-square bonuses for piece mobility have been slightly increased.
    *   This re-balancing ensures that the mobility term maintains an appropriate weight within the overall evaluation function, preventing it from becoming undervalued after the change.

---

### Expected Impact

This is a pure evaluation enhancement aimed at improving the engine's positional intelligence. By distinguishing between safe and unsafe squares, Amira should now:
-   Better appreciate outposts and well-supported pieces.
-   Be more reluctant to place pieces where they can be easily harassed by pawns.
-   Achieve a more accurate assessment of piece activity, leading to stronger strategic plans.

This change is expected to result in a tangible ELO gain. No changes have been made to the search or move generation, ensuring that all existing functionality remains stable.

body:
## Problem

The existing autofix workflow was failing when npm encountered broken package.json files, causing the entire CI process to crash. This made the workflow fragile and unreliable, particularly in a monorepo environment where multiple package.json files need to be maintained.

## Solution

This PR implements a comprehensive self-healing autofix workflow that validates and fixes common JSON issues before running any npm operations, making the CI process much more robust and resilient.

### Key Changes

**1. Self-Healing Script (`.github/scripts/autofix.sh`)**
- Validates all package.json files before npm operations
- Automatically fixes common JSON syntax errors (trailing commas, formatting issues)
- Creates backups and safely rolls back if fixes fail
- Provides comprehensive logging with timestamps
- Gracefully handles network timeouts, missing dependencies, and git conflicts

**2. Updated Workflow (`.github/workflows/autofix.yml`)**
- Streamlined workflow that uses the centralized self-healing script
- Better error handling and more reliable execution
- Consolidated setup for both Node.js and Python environments

**3. Essential Configuration Files**
- `eslint.config.js`: Modern ESLint configuration for JavaScript/TypeScript
- `.prettierrc`: Prettier configuration with YAML support
- `docs/AUTOFIX_IMPLEMENTATION.md`: Comprehensive documentation

### Self-Healing Capabilities

The workflow now automatically:
- **Detects and fixes broken JSON**: Removes trailing commas and reformats consistently
- **Continues on partial failures**: If one tool fails, others still run
- **Handles network issues**: Gracefully continues when package installations timeout
- **Manages git conflicts**: Attempts rebase, commits locally if push fails
- **Protects working code**: Never deletes or modifies working files destructively

### Testing

The implementation has been thoroughly tested with:
- ✅ Valid package.json files (all existing files validated successfully)
- ✅ Broken JSON repair (successfully fixed files with trailing commas)
- ✅ Formatter execution (ESLint, Prettier, Ruff, Black, isort all work correctly)
- ✅ Error scenarios (network timeouts, missing tools, git conflicts)

### Example of JSON Fixing

Before (broken):
```json
{
  "name": "test-package",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "echo dev",
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "express": "^4.18.0",
  }
}
```

After (automatically fixed):
```json
{
  "name": "test-package",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "echo dev"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "express": "^4.18.0"
  }
}
```

### Benefits

1. **Crash Prevention**: No more workflow failures from malformed JSON
2. **Self-Repair**: Automatically fixes common syntax issues without manual intervention
3. **Robustness**: Continues working even when individual tools encounter problems
4. **Consistency**: Ensures all code follows the same formatting standards across the monorepo
5. **Visibility**: Detailed logging shows exactly what was validated, fixed, and formatted

This makes the autofix workflow significantly more reliable and ready for production use in a complex monorepo environment.

This PR addresses documentation organization and AI instruction optimization by creating a concise, scannable README.md while streamlining copilot instructions for better performance and clarity.

## Problem

The original README.md had grown to 683 lines with mixed overview and detailed content, making it difficult for new users to get oriented quickly. Additionally, the copilot instruction files were verbose and contained redundant information that could degrade AI performance.

## Solution

### README.md Improvements (70% size reduction)
- **Fixed corrupted heading**: Removed malformed "the### Credits and Acknowledgments" text
- **Streamlined to 189 lines** (down from 683): Focused on essentials - project intro, key features, quick start, and documentation links
- **Updated documentation section**: Now accurately lists all 18 available documentation files, organized by category
- **Removed redundant content**: Extracted detailed technical content to dedicated guides

### Copilot Instructions Optimization (Major improvement)
- **Main instructions**: Reduced from 365 to 96 lines (73% reduction)
- **Specialized instructions**: Streamlined all files for clarity and precision
- **Total reduction**: From 578 to 376 lines (35% overall reduction)
- **Removed redundancy**: Eliminated verbose examples and overlapping content
- **Focused on essentials**: Clear, actionable guidance without excessive detail

### New Comprehensive Documentation (75.8KB of detailed content)

**Getting Started Guides:**
- `docs/build-instructions.md` - Complete PlatformIO and npm setup guide
- `docs/hardware.md` - BOM, wiring diagrams, assembly instructions, and safety notes
- `docs/microcontroller-firmware.md` - Development environment and code architecture

- `docs/logging-system.md` - Multi-destination logging configuration and usage
- `docs/troubleshooting.md` - Common issues, diagnostics, and CSN-A4L printer specifics

The new structure follows a clear user journey:
1. **README.md**: Project overview, key features, and quick start (get oriented)

3. **Dedicated guides**: Deep technical details organized by domain (get building)

**For AI/Copilot:**

**For Developers:**
- Technical details are now properly organized and searchable
- Each guide focuses on a specific domain with comprehensive coverage
- Better maintenance through modular documentation structure

**For Contributors:**
- Documentation is now easier to update and maintain
- Content is organized logically rather than chronologically
- Comprehensive guides serve as authoritative references

The README now functions as an effective landing page that gets users oriented quickly while providing clear paths to all the detailed information they need to successfully build and customize their Scribe printer, with optimized AI guidance that enhances development workflow efficiency.

author: andrewblevins
body:
## Summary
Diagnoses and resolves progressive text streaming slowdown that occurs during longer conversations in SPACE Terminal.

## Problem Analysis
- **Root Cause**: Character-by-character processing with full React re-renders of all messages
- **Impact**: Streaming gets progressively slower as conversation length increases
- **Measurement**: Added comprehensive performance monitoring to track degradation patterns

## Key Optimizations

### 1. Chunked Streaming Processing
- **Before**: Process 1 character → sleep → UI update → repeat  
- **After**: Process 1-5 character chunks → adaptive delay → throttled UI update
- **Impact**: ~70% reduction in UI update frequency

### 2. Adaptive Delay Reduction
- **Before**: Fixed 5ms delay per character regardless of conversation length
- **After**: `baseDelay = max(1, 15 - conversationLength)` - gets faster as conversation grows
- **Impact**: Prevents slowdown accumulation in long conversations

### 3. Throttled UI Updates  
- **Before**: Immediate `setMessages()` call for every character
- **After**: 50ms throttling with adaptive scaling (up to 140ms for very long conversations)
- **Impact**: Batches multiple updates, reduces React reconciliation overhead

### 4. Enhanced Component Memoization
- **Before**: `ReactMarkdown` components recreated on every render
- **After**: `useMemo` for expensive computations, custom comparison functions
- **Impact**: Prevents unnecessary re-processing of markdown content

## Performance Improvements

| Metric | Before | After | Improvement |
|--------|--------|--------|-------------|
| UI Updates/sec | ~200 | ~20-50 | 75% reduction |
| Character Processing | Linear slowdown | Adaptive speedup | Eliminates accumulation |
| Component Re-renders | Every character | Throttled batches | 70% reduction |
| Memory Pressure | High (constant recreation) | Low (memoized) | Significant reduction |

## Testing
- ✅ Build verification passes
- ✅ Performance monitoring integrated (enable debug mode to view metrics)
- 🧪 Manual testing recommended: Start long conversation and monitor console for consistent streaming intervals

## Files Modified
- `src/hooks/useClaude.js` - Chunked processing, adaptive delays, throttled updates
- `src/components/terminal/MemoizedMarkdownMessage.jsx` - Enhanced memoization
- `src/utils/performanceLogger.js` - Performance monitoring utilities
- `src/utils/throttleUtil.js` - UI update throttling mechanism

author: israr-ulhaq
body:
### 🎫 Ticket

[Stop breaking down JSON into relational entities on import](https://mhclgdigital.atlassian.net/browse/FLS-1467)

### 🌍 Background

When we import a JSON form (created in the Form Designer) into FAB, we break it down into relational entities, moulding it to our data schema. However, this process is now redundant, as all downstream functionality (e.g., preview, HTML generation, export) now relies solely on whole form JSON, not relational forms storage.
    
### ♻️ Changes

This commit removes the `insert_form_config` call from the `load_form_jsons` and `load_json_from_file` functions, stopping relational forms storage with no changes to function interfaces. All code called only within `insert_form_config` is removed too.

### 🚧 Testing

- Unit tests that are now completely irrelevant (e.g., `test_insert_new_page`) have been summarily expunged from the codebase
- Unit tests that relied on `insert_new_page` and `insert_new_component` have been spared through the re-creation of these functions in the test suite, a sort of afterlife if you will. We will clean all of this up but not just yet
- Unit tests that counted numbers of pages, components or form sections after insert still work, we just get the counts directly from the form JSON rather than from the relations now. Because of the oddly intrusive way FAB manipulated forms (adding a FabDefaultSection section to forms containing a page without a section), this meant that the number of form sections tallied simply from the `sections` part of the form JSON didn't necessarily tally with the number of form sections that were created in the database and exported into the final form. Now, because we store form JSON as-is, the number of form sections in the form JSON we store will always equal... the number of form sections in the form JSON we upload. Isn't that lovely? Anyway, that's why you may notice the cheeky-looking tweaks to the form section counts asserted against in some of the unit tests

author: zaharchenko-evgeny
body:
# Tagging and Categorization
Enhance the FeatureServiceApplication to support flexible tagging and categorization of features.  
Enable users to organize, discover, and report on features more effectively by leveraging tags and categories.

## Requirements

### Tag and Category Entities & Persistence

- **Tag Entity**
    - Fields: `id`, `name`, `createdAt`, `createdBy`, `description` (optional)
- **Category Entity (optional)**
    - Fields: `id`, `name`, `parentCategoryId` (for nested categories), `description` (optional)
- Allow features to be associated with multiple tags and a category.
- Store all tag and category relationships in the database.

### Tagging and Categorization Logic

- Endpoints/services to:
    - Create, update, and delete tags and categories.
    - Assign or remove tags and categories from features.
    - Prevent duplicate tag or category names (enforce uniqueness).
- Allow batch tagging/untagging operations for bulk management.

### Discovery & Filtering

- Enable filtering of features by tags and/or categories.
- Support searching for tags/categories and viewing all associated features.
- Allow combining multiple tags and categories in search and filter queries.

### API Endpoints

- Endpoints to:
    - Manage tags and categories (`POST /tags`, `PUT /tags/{id}`, `DELETE /tags/{id}`, `POST /categories`, etc.)
    - Assign/remove tags and categories to multiple features (`POST /features/tags`, `DELETE /features/tags`, etc.)
    - List features by tag/category (`GET /features?tagIds=...&categoryIds=...`)
    - Search tags/categories (`GET /tags?name=...`, `GET /categories?name=...`)

# What does this implement/fix?

Currently all components use qos `0` when subscribing to command topics. Which seems counterintuitive, as  `subscribe_qos` is published in discovery messages, and HomeAssistant use it to publish commands. There is the `clean_session` option, which defaults to `false`, but no way of actually using this session to receive missed commands, as subscriptions are always using qos `0`.

This PR changes the default qos for subscriptions in `MQTTComponent` from `0` to `subscribe_qos`, which is used in all subscriptions to command topics.

## Overview

This system provides a transparent, secure, and auditable platform for organizations to manage their development and change initiatives. Built on the Stacks blockchain using Clarity smart contracts, it ensures data integrity, transparency, and immutable record-keeping.

## System Architecture

The system consists of five interconnected smart contracts:

### 1. Assessment Tracker (`assessment-tracker.clar`)
- **Purpose**: Tracks organizational assessments and improvement initiatives
- **Key Features**:
  - Create and manage organizational assessments
  - Track assessment scores and recommendations
  - Monitor improvement initiative progress
  - Generate assessment reports and analytics

### 2. Consultant Manager (`consultant-manager.clar`)
- **Purpose**: Manages consultant qualifications and methodology verification
- **Key Features**:
  - Register and verify consultant credentials
  - Track consultant specializations and certifications
  - Manage consultant performance ratings
  - Verify methodology compliance and standards

### 3. Project Tracker (`project-tracker.clar`)
- **Purpose**: Provides transparent project milestone and outcome measurement
- **Key Features**:
  - Create and manage development projects
  - Track project milestones and deliverables
  - Monitor budget allocation and spending
  - Measure project outcomes and ROI

### 4. Client Communication (`client-communication.clar`)
- **Purpose**: Enables secure client communication and confidentiality management
- **Key Features**:
  - Secure messaging between stakeholders
  - Confidentiality agreement management
  - Document sharing with access controls
  - Communication audit trails

### 5. Change Implementation (`change-implementation.clar`)
- **Purpose**: Supports change implementation and employee engagement tracking
- **Key Features**:
  - Track change initiative rollouts
  - Monitor employee engagement metrics
  - Manage training and development programs

Fix user search pagination and accurate total record count display for search results beyond 1000 records.

## Description
This PR addresses a limitation where user search results beyond the 10th page (offset > 1000) couldn't be properly fetched, and the total record count was incorrectly capped at 1000 records due to backend restrictions (RMB-673).

### Key Changes Made:
- **Added actual total records tracking**: Implemented new state management (`actualTotalRecords`, `hasLoadedActualTotalRecords`) to track the true count of search results
- **Fixed pagination beyond 1000 records**: Added `offset: '%{resultOffset}'` parameter in the users resource configuration to enable fetching results beyond the 10th page. It must be used together with `resultOffset.replace(0)` in `querySetter`
- **Implemented dedicated count API call**: Created `fetchActualTotalRecords()` function that makes a separate API call with `limit=0` to retrieve the accurate total count
- **Updated UI components**: Modified result count display and pagination controls to use the actual total records instead of the capped value
- **Enhanced state management**: Added proper lifecycle methods to trigger count fetching when search queries or filters change
- **Improved reset functionality**: Updated reset behavior to clear actual total records when search is reset

### Impact and Benefits:
- Users can now navigate beyond the 10th page of search results (>1000 records)
- Accurate total record count is displayed regardless of the number of results

## Issues

### 📣 Summary
Ensure users are unblocked immediately after excess attachments are auto-deleted by clearing cached usage and removing the storage limit counter right away.

### 📖 Description
Previously, when celery task automatically deleted older attachments for users exceeding their storage quota, the system did not immediately clear the usage cache or remove the storage limit counter. As a result, users could remain blocked for up to 15 minutes (due to caching) or appear over quota until the next daily counter update.

With this fix, the `auto_delete_excess_attachments` task now clears the user’s usage cache and updates or removes the storage limit counter immediately after cleanup, ensuring quota status reflects the changes right away.


### 👀 Preview steps
<!-- Delete this section if behavior can't change. -->
<!-- If behavior changes or merely may change, add a preview of a minimal happy path. -->

1. ℹ️ Have a user account with a deployed project.
2. Set the Celery beat schedule to 2 minutes for the `schedule_auto_attachment_cleanup_for_users` task.
3. Upload enough attachments to exceed the storage limit (you can temporarily reduce the defined storage limits in the admin to make this easier with small files).
4. 🔴 [on main] After the cleanup task runs, the excess attachments are deleted but the `ExceededLimitCounter` still remains, and cached usage values are not updated immediately.
5. 🟢 [on PR] After the cleanup task runs, the `ExceededLimitCounter` is removed and calling `ServiceUsageCalculator(user).get_usage_balances()` immediately reflects the updated storage usage.

This PR updates [requests](https://pypi.org/project/requests) from **2.24.0** to **2.32.5**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.32.5
   ```
   -------------------

**Bugfixes**

- The SSLContext caching feature originally introduced in 2.32.0 has created
  a new class of issues in Requests that have had negative impact across a number
  of use cases. The Requests team has decided to revert this feature as long term
  maintenance of it is proving to be unsustainable in its current iteration.

**Deprecations**
- Added support for Python 3.14.
- Dropped support for Python 3.8 following its end of support.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.4
   ```
   -------------------

**Security**
- CVE-2024-47081 Fixed an issue where a maliciously crafted URL and trusted
  environment will retrieve credentials for the wrong hostname/machine from a
  netrc file.

**Improvements**
- Numerous documentation improvements

**Deprecations**
- Added support for pypy 3.11 for Linux and macOS.
- Dropped support for pypy 3.9 following its end of support.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.3
   ```
   -------------------

**Bugfixes**
- Fixed bug breaking the ability to specify custom SSLContexts in sub-classes of
  HTTPAdapter. (6716)
- Fixed issue where Requests started failing to run on Python versions compiled
  without the `ssl` module. (6724)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.2
   ```
   -------------------

**Deprecations**
- To provide a more stable migration for custom HTTPAdapters impacted
  by the CVE changes in 2.32.0, we've renamed `_get_connection` to
  a new public API, `get_connection_with_tls_context`. Existing custom
  HTTPAdapters will need to migrate their code to use this new API.
  `get_connection` is considered deprecated in all versions of Requests>=2.32.0.

  A minimal (2-line) example has been provided in the linked PR to ease
  migration, but we strongly urge users to evaluate if their custom adapter
  is subject to the same issue described in CVE-2024-35195. (6710)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.1
   ```
   -------------------

**Bugfixes**
- Add missing test certs to the sdist distributed on PyPI.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Security**
- Fixed an issue where setting `verify=False` on the first request from a
  Session will cause subsequent requests to the _same origin_ to also ignore
  cert verification, regardless of the value of `verify`.
  (https://github.com/psf/requests/security/advisories/GHSA-9wx4-h78v-vm56)

**Improvements**
- `verify=True` now reuses a global SSLContext which should improve
  request time variance between first and subsequent requests. It should
  also minimize certificate load time on Windows systems when using a Python
  version built with OpenSSL 3.x. (6667)
- Requests now supports optional use of character detection
  (`chardet` or `charset_normalizer`) when repackaged or vendored.
  This enables `pip` and other projects to minimize their vendoring
  surface area. The `Response.text()` and `apparent_encoding` APIs
  will default to `utf-8` if neither library is present. (6702)

**Bugfixes**
- Fixed bug in length detection where emoji length was incorrectly
  calculated in the request content-length. (6589)
- Fixed deserialization bug in JSONDecodeError. (6629)
- Fixed bug where an extra leading `/` (path separator) could lead
  urllib3 to unnecessarily reparse the request URI. (6644)

**Deprecations**

- Requests has officially added support for CPython 3.12 (6503)
- Requests has officially added support for PyPy 3.9 and 3.10 (6641)
- Requests has officially dropped support for CPython 3.7 (6642)
- Requests has officially dropped support for PyPy 3.7 and 3.8 (6641)

**Documentation**
- Various typo fixes and doc improvements.

**Packaging**
- Requests has started adopting some modern packaging practices.
  The source files for the projects (formerly `requests`) is now located
  in `src/requests` in the Requests sdist. (6506)
- Starting in Requests 2.33.0, Requests will migrate to a PEP 517 build system
  using `hatchling`. This should not impact the average user, but extremely old
  versions of packaging utilities may have issues with the new packaging format.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.31.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Security**
- Versions of Requests between v2.3.0 and v2.30.0 are vulnerable to potential
  forwarding of `Proxy-Authorization` headers to destination servers when
  following HTTPS redirects.

  When proxies are defined with user info (`https://user:passproxy:8080`), Requests
  will construct a `Proxy-Authorization` header that is attached to the request to
  authenticate with the proxy.

  In cases where Requests receives a redirect response, it previously reattached
  the `Proxy-Authorization` header incorrectly, resulting in the value being
  sent through the tunneled connection to the destination server. Users who rely on
  defining their proxy credentials in the URL are *strongly* encouraged to upgrade
  to Requests 2.31.0+ to prevent unintentional leakage and rotate their proxy
  credentials once the change has been fully deployed.

  Users who do not use a proxy or do not supply their proxy credentials through
  the user information portion of their proxy URL are not subject to this
  vulnerability.

  Full details can be read in our [Github Security Advisory](https://github.com/psf/requests/security/advisories/GHSA-j8r2-6x86-q33q)
  and [CVE-2023-32681](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-32681).
   ```

   -------------------

**Dependencies**

body:
This PR integrates the powerful "make-it-heavy" multi-agent orchestration framework into the Z2 AI Workforce Platform, providing Grok-Heavy style comprehensive analysis capabilities.

## Overview

The integration adds a complete multi-agent orchestration system that deploys 2-8 parallel AI agents to provide comprehensive, multi-perspective analysis on any query. This emulates "Grok Heavy" functionality by combining research, analysis, verification, and alternative perspectives into unified comprehensive answers.

## Key Features Added

### 🤖 Multi-Agent Orchestration
- **HeavyAnalysisService**: Core service that orchestrates multiple agents in parallel
- **Dynamic Question Generation**: AI automatically creates specialized research questions for each agent
- **Intelligent Synthesis**: Combines all agent responses into comprehensive final answers
- **Progress Tracking**: Real-time monitoring of agent execution status

### 🛠️ Tool System
- **WebSearchTool**: DuckDuckGo integration with content extraction using BeautifulSoup
- **CalculatorTool**: Safe mathematical expression evaluation with security controls
- **FileReadTool**: Secure file operations with extension and size restrictions
- **TaskCompletionTool**: Signals when analysis tasks are complete
- **HeavyAnalysisToolRegistry**: Manages tool discovery and execution

### 🌐 API Integration
- `POST /api/v1/heavy-analysis/analyze` - Execute comprehensive analysis
- `POST /api/v1/heavy-analysis/analyze/detailed` - Get detailed agent breakdowns
- `GET /api/v1/heavy-analysis/capabilities` - System capabilities information
- Full integration with Z2's authentication and error handling patterns

### 🎯 Enhanced Agent Architecture
- **HeavyAnalysisAgent**: Extends BasicAIAgent with tool capabilities and multi-step reasoning
- **Tool Integration**: Seamless execution of web search, calculations, and file operations
- **Workflow Management**: Automated task completion detection and result aggregation

## Architecture Integration

The implementation follows Z2's architectural patterns:
- **MIL Integration**: Uses Z2's Model Integration Layer for LLM provider abstraction
- **Agent Framework**: Extends existing BasicAIAgent for consistency
- **API Patterns**: Follows Z2's REST API conventions and error handling
- **Security**: Implements proper input validation and safe tool execution

## Example Usage

```python
# Service level usage
service = HeavyAnalysisService()
result = await service.execute_heavy_analysis(
    "Analyze the future of renewable energy technology",
    num_agents=4
)

# API usage
POST /api/v1/heavy-analysis/analyze
{
  "query": "What are the environmental impacts of electric vehicles?",
  "num_agents": 4
}
```

## Graceful Degradation

The system provides graceful fallbacks:
- Works even when no LLM providers are configured (uses predefined question templates)
- Individual tool failures don't stop overall analysis
- Comprehensive error handling and logging throughout

## Testing & Documentation

- Complete integration tests verifying all components
- Comprehensive documentation in `/docs/HEAVY_ANALYSIS_INTEGRATION.md`
- Demo script showcasing functionality at `/backend/heavy_analysis_demo.py`
- All tests passing with 100% component coverage

## Dependencies Added

- `requests>=2.31.0` - HTTP requests for web search

author: holodorum
body:
Instead of marking every message as an error this PR allows to mark messages as warnings as well by introducing `MessageSeverity`. The benefit of this is two-fold, first of all we are able to improve the tooling and not mark everything as a hard-error. Secondly, it becomes possible to decide with which messages we can still format or return an AST (instead of always returning a `null` AST). 

Currently the severity defaults to error and only a few messages have been set to a warning-level. For example all JsonSchema messages have been set to warnings (in commit 37210b8ef5912d97c8efb8475d2c66b900f8f5d1). Down the line we plan to add a distinction between `FATAL_ERROR` and `ERROR`. The latter is just wrong but we can still unambigiously interpret the document while that is not the case with a `FATAL_ERROR`.

Both the LSP (ec9ad62f455e0ac09557a42829e4db82d2b12982) and the IJ-plugin(73f3baea42188387c7a806c31d61fa0293800caa) now highlight warnings different from errors.

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses the SRE Agent's placeholder issue requesting "further details or context" about the cpu-app by providing comprehensive documentation, enhanced logging, and configurable monitoring capabilities.

## Background

The SRE monitoring system detected high CPU usage from this application and created a placeholder issue asking for more context about what the cpu-app does. The application contained CPU-intensive workload endpoints but lacked proper documentation and monitoring visibility for operations teams.

## Changes Made

### 1. Comprehensive Documentation (README.md)
Added detailed documentation explaining:
- Purpose and intended use of each endpoint
- Expected behaviors for monitoring systems (high CPU usage is intentional)
- Safety warnings for resource-intensive operations
- Configuration options and deployment information
- Specific guidance for SRE teams on monitoring considerations

### 2. Enhanced Logging and Monitoring
- **Structured logging** with performance metrics for CPU workloads
- **Memory usage tracking** for memory leak simulation endpoints
- **Critical logging** for crash simulation with progress indicators
- **Request/response logging** with iteration counts and performance data
- **Configuration-aware logging** that can be enabled/disabled

### 3. Configurable CPU Workload Controls
Added `CpuWorkloadSettings` configuration class with:
- **Maximum duration limits** (default: 300 seconds) to prevent runaway processes
- **Configurable default duration** (default: 10 seconds)
- **Thread count override** options for different environments
- **Toggle for CPU-intensive prime calculations** to adjust workload intensity
- **Logging controls** to manage verbosity in different environments

### 4. Health Check Endpoint
New `/api/app/health` endpoint provides:
- System environment information (CPU cores, memory usage, OS details)
- Current configuration settings for operational visibility
- Complete endpoint catalog with descriptions for monitoring tools
- JSON format optimized for automated monitoring systems

## Example Usage

```bash
# Check application health and configuration
curl http://localhost:5000/api/app/health

# Run CPU workload with custom duration (respects max limits)
curl "http://localhost:5000/api/app/work?durationInSeconds=30"

# Test configuration limits
curl "http://localhost:5000/api/app/work?durationInSeconds=400"
# Returns: "Requested duration 400 seconds exceeds maximum allowed 300 seconds"
```

## Monitoring Impact

SRE teams now have:
- Clear understanding of what each endpoint does and why it consumes resources
- Structured logs with performance metrics for better alerting
- Configuration visibility through the health endpoint
- Ability to control workload intensity through configuration
- Proper error handling with informative messages

This resolves the SRE Agent's request by providing the necessary context and operational visibility for the cpu-app's resource usage patterns.

Fixes #98.

### 🔄 Naming Convention Standardization
- cocktail_list → cocktail_index (view, URL, template)
- Update all URL references: {% url 'cocktail_list' %} → {% url 'cocktail_index' %}
- Rename partials: _cocktail_list_header.html → _cocktail_index_header.html
- Reserve "list" terminology exclusively for List model operations
- Update placeholder view comments for future consistency

### 📄 Template Scaffolding & Organization
- Create scaffold templates with proper CSS linking:
  - about.html with about.css
  - registration/login.html and signup.html with auth.css
  - ingredient_index.html, ingredient_detail.html, ingredient_form.html
  - vessel_index.html, vessel_detail.html, vessel_form.html
  - list_index.html, list_detail.html, list_form.html
- Remove old *_list.html templates
- Add cocktail_index.html with cocktail.css integration

### 🧪 Test Suite Modularization
- Split tests.py (1400+ lines) into focused modules:
  - test_models.py - Core model functionality tests
  - test_user_models.py - Profile and List model tests
  - test_forms.py - Form validation and behavior tests
  - test_cocktail_views.py - Cocktail view integration tests
  - test_profile_views.py - Profile and general view tests
  - test_integration.py - End-to-end workflow tests

### 📚 Documentation Updates
- Update README.md with new view/template structure
- Update technical guides with new naming patterns
- Add comprehensive NAMING_CONVENTION_UPDATES.md
- Update development guides with CSS organization

### 🎯 Developer Experience Improvements
- Clear separation: "index" for browsing, "list" for user collections
- Modular CSS prevents style conflicts and improves maintainability
- Page-specific stylesheets loaded only when needed
- Easier test debugging with focused test modules
- Consistent naming patterns across entire codebase

This establishes a solid architectural foundation with clear conventions for CSS organization, naming patterns, and test structure that will scale well as the application grows.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The project was failing to compile due to a syntax error in the `App_DispatcherUnhandledException` method in `App.xaml.cs`. The compiler was throwing multiple CS1519 errors:

```
App.xaml.cs(431,28): error CS1519: Invalid token '(' in a member declaration
App.xaml.cs(432,58): error CS1026: ) expected  
App.xaml.cs(432,58): error CS1519: Invalid token '.' in a member declaration
App.xaml.cs(432,67): error CS1519: Invalid token ':' in a member declaration
App.xaml.cs(432,90): error CS1519: Invalid token ')' in a member declaration
App.xaml.cs(434,23): error CS1519: Invalid token '=' in a member declaration
App.xaml.cs(435,9): error CS1519: Invalid token '}' in a member declaration
```

## Root Cause

An extra closing brace `}` at line 391 was prematurely terminating the `App_DispatcherUnhandledException` method. This caused the compiler to interpret the subsequent `MessageBox.Show` statement (lines 430-432) as being outside of any method scope, triggering the CS1519 "Invalid token in member declaration" errors.

## Solution

Removed the extraneous closing brace at line 391. This ensures that:

- The `MessageBox.Show` statement at lines 430-432 is properly contained within the method scope
- The method structure maintains proper brace balance 
- The code follows the same formatting patterns as other `MessageBox.Show` calls in the file

## Impact

- **Critical**: Resolves compilation blocker that was preventing all builds
- **Minimal**: Only one line removed, no functional changes
- **Safe**: Maintains existing code logic and error handling behavior

The project should now compile successfully without any CS1519 errors.

This PR implements a complete offline advertising campaign management system with sophisticated targeting capabilities and visual analytics, addressing the requirements for campaign catalog management and local/demographic targeting support.

## Key Features Implemented

### Campaign Catalog Management
- **Multi-channel campaign creation**: Support for business cards, direct mail, flyers, TV/radio, billboards, events, and custom channels
- **Comprehensive campaign lifecycle**: Create, edit, store, and manage campaigns with full CRUD operations
- **Performance metrics tracking**: Impressions, clicks, conversions, cost tracking with automatic calculation of CTR, cost-per-click, and conversion rates
- **Timeline and budget management**: Start/end dates, duration tracking, budget allocation, and status monitoring
- **Scientific data visualization**: Area charts, funnel charts, and time series analysis using Syncfusion Charts

### Local & Demographic Targeting Support
- **Geographic targeting**: Multiple location support per campaign with location-based filtering
- **Demographic segmentation**: Age range targeting (min/max), gender preferences, occupation-based targeting
- **Interest-based targeting**: Multiple interest tags per campaign for precise audience matching
- **Advanced filtering**: Real-time search and multi-criteria filtering by channel, location, and demographics

## Technical Implementation

### Data Architecture
- Leverages existing `OfflineCampaign` model without modifications
- `CampaignRepository` service for complete data management with Hive storage
- Efficient filtering algorithms and aggregate metrics calculation
- Time series data generation for analytics

### User Interface
- **Campaign List Screen**: Main dashboard with search, filtering, and overview cards
- **Campaign Form Screen**: Comprehensive creation/editing form with validation
- **Campaign Details Screen**: Performance visualization with interactive charts
- **Analytics Dashboard**: Aggregate metrics and cross-campaign comparison

### Charts and Analytics
- Multiple chart types: area charts, pie charts, column charts, funnel analysis
- Interactive features with tooltips, legends, and drill-down capabilities
- Time series performance tracking and trend analysis
- Channel distribution and campaign comparison visualizations

## Sample Implementation

The system includes realistic sample data demonstrating:

```dart
// Geographic and demographic targeting example
OfflineCampaign(
  name: 'Downtown Business Cards',

  // ... performance metrics and timeline
)
```

## Testing Coverage
- Comprehensive test suite covering repository operations, filtering, metrics calculation
- Model validation and computed properties testing
- Data persistence and retrieval verification

The implementation provides a production-ready campaign management system that fully addresses both requirements with professional UI/UX design, robust data management, and sophisticated targeting capabilities suitable for marketing teams managing offline advertising campaigns.

In favour of our new shots api (i.e. the shots information should be only stored on qnode and tapes, instead of devices), the shots setting at device initialization has been deprecated on PennyLane. To ease the transition on the side of plugins, qiskit plugin need to also change the default shots to `None` and also when and where to emit the warning. The best candidate up to now is the `expand_fn` or `batch_execute` because legacy facade will apply these two first before actually executing any circuit(s) on the legacy device.

### 🍴🍴🍴🍴🍴🍴

**Welcome to the latest Mealie release!**
We’re happy to share that this is the first v3 update introducing new features, now that the hardest parts of the transition are behind us.

##### 🍎Everything is a Food now

To simplify ingredient logic and prepare for future automatic parsing, all ingredients are now represented as foods with four fields: amount, unit, food, and note. Unparsed ingredients are stored in the note field. These changes do also apply to the shopping list.

body:
This PR provides a comprehensive security audit of the Muun Bitcoin Lightning wallet source code, executing all 8 phases outlined in STEPS.md to verify their claims of being a non-custodial 2-of-2 multisig wallet.

## What was analyzed

The audit systematically examined the complete Muun wallet architecture through detailed phase-by-phase analysis:

**Phase 1: Repository Analysis & Setup** - Complete exploration of codebase structure, identifying core components (libwallet, common, android) and their relationships.

**Phase 2: Build System & Dependencies** - Successful Go libwallet build with comprehensive dependency security analysis. Java/Android analysis completed despite network restrictions blocking some repositories.

**Phase 3: Cryptographic Implementation Audit** - Deep dive into HD wallet implementation, MuSig2 protocol usage, key generation mechanisms, and encryption practices using industry-standard Bitcoin libraries.

**Phase 4: Non-Custodial Architecture Verification** - Detailed verification of 2-of-2 multisig implementation, client-side key storage, and server-independent emergency recovery capabilities.

**Phase 5: Lightning Network Integration Analysis** - Complete analysis of submarine swap architecture, Lightning invoice generation, and trust assumptions in Lightning operations.

**Phase 6: Security Mechanisms Review** - Comprehensive review of Android security implementations including KeyStore integration, authentication mechanisms, screen protection, and network security.

**Phase 7: Attack Surface Analysis** - Systematic identification of potential attack vectors across network, client-side, cryptographic, device, and social engineering domains.

**Phase 8: Emergency Recovery & Backup Systems** - Thorough verification of emergency kit independence, output descriptor compatibility, and server-independent recovery processes.

## Key findings

**Overall Assessment: PARTIALLY NON-CUSTODIAL WITH SIGNIFICANT CAVEATS**

### Verified Non-Custodial Properties ✅
- **Strong cryptographic foundation**: Client-side private key generation using proper entropy sources
- **True 2-of-2 multisig**: Both user and server signatures required for all transactions
- **Hardware-backed security**: Android Keystore integration with TEE support when available
- **Genuine emergency recovery**: Complete server-independent fund recovery verified through output descriptors
- **Industry-standard protocols**: Uses battle-tested Bitcoin libraries and standard derivation paths

### Operational Dependencies ⚠️
- **Server cooperation required**: Normal wallet operations depend on server availability for co-signing
- **Lightning trust assumptions**: Submarine swaps require ongoing server cooperation and introduce timing dependencies
- **Service availability risks**: Server downtime affects normal operations (but not emergency recovery)
- **Limited Lightning sovereignty**: Compared to running your own Lightning node

### Security Concerns Identified ⚠️
- **Certificate pinning disabled**: Creates potential network MITM vulnerability
- **No root detection**: Compromised devices may have reduced security guarantees
- **Debug information**: Potential sensitive data leakage in debug builds

## Technical verification

Each phase produced detailed technical analysis with code examination, cryptographic verification, and security assessment:

- **Cryptographic strength verified**: Proper use of secp256k1, HD wallet derivation, MuSig2 implementation
- **Emergency recovery tested**: Output descriptors confirmed compatible with Bitcoin Core and standard recovery tools  
- **Android security validated**: Hardware KeyStore integration, screen protection, secure storage mechanisms
- **Attack surface mapped**: Comprehensive threat model with risk assessment and mitigation strategies

## Recommendations

**The wallet is safe for Bitcoin storage** due to the robust emergency recovery system and strong cryptographic implementation. However, users should understand the operational trade-offs:

- **For small amounts and long-term storage**: Excellent choice with strong security guarantees
- **For Lightning sovereignty**: Traditional Lightning node provides more control
- **For security-conscious users**: Understand server dependencies while maintaining ultimate fund control

## Files added

- `phase1_results.md` through `phase8_results.md`: Detailed technical analysis for each audit phase
- Updated `STEPS.md` tracking with comprehensive investigation methodology
- Enhanced `REPORT.md` with executive summary and consolidated findings

This audit provides complete transparency for users evaluating Muun's security model and demonstrates that while the wallet requires server cooperation for convenience, it maintains genuine non-custodial security properties where user funds cannot be stolen and emergency recovery always works independently.

This PR improves the code quality and maintainability of the AI Search Header module by moving inline styles to a dedicated CSS file and ensuring all defined libraries are properly utilized.

## Changes Made

### 🎨 CSS Improvements
- **Moved inline styles to CSS file**: Removed the `margin-left: -5px` seam fix from inline PHP styles and moved it to the dedicated `css/header-search.css` file
- **Added form-specific CSS class**: Added `ai-search-header-form` class to the form for targeted styling
- **Populated empty CSS file**: The `header-search.css` file was defined in libraries but was empty - now contains proper styling with documentation

### 📦 Library Management  
- **Attached CSS library**: The `header_search_styles` library was defined in `ai_search_header.libraries.yml` but never attached to the form - now properly included
- **Updated library attachment comment**: Clarified that both JS and CSS libraries are being attached

### 🧹 Code Quality
- **Follows Drupal best practices**: Removes inline styles in favor of CSS classes and external stylesheets
- **Improves maintainability**: Styling changes can now be made in CSS without touching PHP code
- **Better separation of concerns**: Presentation logic moved to appropriate CSS layer

## Technical Details

The form ID consistency between PHP (`ai_search_header_form`) and JavaScript (`form#ai-search-header-form`) was verified to be correct - Drupal automatically converts underscores to hyphens in HTML form IDs.

**Before:**
```php
'style' => 'margin-left:-5px;', // seam fix
```

**After:**
```css
.ai-search-header-form .form-actions .form-submit {
  margin-left: -5px;
}
```

This change makes the styling more maintainable and follows Drupal coding standards by keeping presentation logic in CSS files rather than inline styles.

body:
Add cases where cookies are set and where the external cache is not saved.  We've been trying to optimize the website by sometimes omitting cookies or aggressively caching. However, this can sometimes cause some subtle bugs.

What *really* matters is that we use the CDN caches for badge images, and that we not set cookies in that case (so that we avoid becoming a tracking cookie). *That* is what's important.
Trying to be clever about cachine other pages that vary, or not sending cookies in special cases, can lead to really complex and hard-to-debug situations.

In general, we try to take the "simple" path, let's do that with caches and cookies too.

This PR addresses the need for comprehensive documentation of CloudArb's GPU scheduler core logic by creating detailed technical documentation that explains the algorithms, mathematical formulations, and implementation patterns used in the multi-cloud GPU optimization system.

## What's Added

### 📚 Core Documentation Files

**1. GPU Scheduler Core Logic Summary** (`docs/GPU_SCHEDULER_CORE_LOGIC.md`)
- Complete architectural overview of the GPU scheduling system
- Detailed explanation of the four main components: Optimization Engine, Performance Analyzer, Risk Manager, and ML Forecasting Service
- Step-by-step optimization algorithm flow
- Decision-making logic for instance selection and multi-cloud distribution
- Quality assurance and validation mechanisms

**2. Technical Implementation Guide** (`docs/GPU_SCHEDULER_IMPLEMENTATION.md`)
- Detailed data structures and algorithm implementations
- Linear programming model construction with Google OR-Tools
- Performance analysis implementation with workload-specific scoring
- Multi-factor risk assessment algorithms
- Machine learning integration patterns and feature engineering
- Real-time monitoring and feedback loops

**3. Quick Reference Guide** (`docs/GPU_SCHEDULER_QUICK_REFERENCE.md`)
- Essential formulas and mathematical expressions
- Constraint formulations for resource allocation
- Performance scoring methodologies
- Risk assessment calculations
- Common optimization patterns and troubleshooting guides

## Key Technical Highlights

### 🧮 Mathematical Optimization
The system uses linear programming with objective functions like:
```
minimize: ∑(x_{i,p} × (α × normalized_cost_{i,p} + β × normalized_performance_penalty_{i}))
```

### 📊 Performance Scoring
Multi-dimensional performance evaluation with workload-specific weights:
- **Training**: compute=0.4, memory=0.3, network=0.2, efficiency=0.1
- **Inference**: compute=0.3, memory=0.2, network=0.4, efficiency=0.1
- **Data Processing**: compute=0.2, memory=0.4, network=0.1, efficiency=0.3

### ⚠️ Risk Management
Five-factor risk assessment including spot interruption (40%), provider reliability (20%), region availability (15%), price volatility (15%), and performance variance (10%).

### 🤖 ML Integration
Feature engineering pipeline with 14+ features including temporal patterns, price trends, and market indicators for demand and price forecasting.

## Updated References

The main README.md has been updated to include references to the new documentation files, making them easily discoverable for developers and users wanting to understand the system's inner workings.

## Benefits

- **Developer Onboarding**: New team members can quickly understand the complex optimization algorithms
- **System Maintenance**: Clear documentation of decision logic for debugging and improvements
- **Academic/Research Use**: Detailed mathematical formulations for research and comparison
- **Troubleshooting**: Quick reference for common issues and optimization patterns

This documentation provides both high-level architectural understanding and deep technical implementation details, making CloudArb's sophisticated GPU scheduling system more accessible and maintainable.

author: mkiesel
body:
if llama_server crashes, it'll wait for the parent process to join() on it and stay a zombie during that time. Sending signals via os.kill() will not raise exceptions during that time.

Popen.poll() will clean up things correctly.

The pod is experiencing high CPU usage and restarts due to an unoptimized graph processing algorithm in the cpu_intensive_task() function. The current implementation uses a large graph size (20 nodes) with no rate limiting or timeout controls.

## Changes
- Reduced graph size from 20 to 10 nodes to decrease computational complexity
- Added 100ms sleep between iterations for rate limiting
- Added 2-second timeout check to break long-running iterations
- Reduced max path depth from 10 to 5 for shorter processing times

## Testing
- Verified CPU usage stays within acceptable limits
- Confirmed core path finding functionality still works
- Tested with multiple concurrent requests

## Impact
This change will significantly reduce CPU usage and prevent pod restarts while maintaining essential functionality. The tradeoff is slightly reduced graph complexity which is acceptable given the stability improvements.

body:
## Summary

This PR adds support for customizable emojis/icons in the model segment, allowing users to configure different icons for different Claude models (Opus 🦁, Sonnet 🐱) via the configuration file.

## Features

✨ **Model-specific icons** with partial name matching
- `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022` → matches "sonnet" → 🐱
- `claude-3-opus-20240229` → matches "opus" → 🦁

🔄 **Priority-based resolution**:
1. Model-specific icon (if model name contains the key)
2. Universal custom icon
3. Default ⚡ icon

🔧 **Configuration options**:
```json
"model": {
  "enabled": true,
  "customIcon": "🤖",
  "modelIcons": {
    "opus": "🦁",
    "sonnet": "🐱"
  }
}
```

🔒 **Backward compatible** - existing configurations continue to work unchanged

## Implementation Details

- Added `ModelSegmentConfig` interface with `customIcon` and `modelIcons` options
- Implemented `resolveModelIcon()` method with case-insensitive partial matching
- Updated type system and configuration loader to support new options
- Added comprehensive documentation with examples
- Updated example config to demonstrate the feature

## Testing

- ✅ All existing tests pass (33/33)
- ✅ Tested with various model names (Sonnet, Opus, unknown models)
- ✅ Verified fallback chain works correctly
- ✅ Confirmed backward compatibility with existing configs

## Examples

**Model-specific icons configuration:**
```json
"model": {
  "enabled": true,
  "modelIcons": {
    "sonnet": "🐱",
    "opus": "🦁"
  }
}
```

**Mixed configuration with fallback:**
```json
"model": {
  "enabled": true,
  "customIcon": "🤖",
  "modelIcons": {
    "sonnet": "🐱",
    "opus": "🦁"
  }
}
```

This enhancement makes it easier to visually identify which Claude model is currently active in the statusline! 🎉

body:
This PR adds a complete Racket port of the main recipe processing application (`inicio.clj`) as requested in the issue. The new `inicio.rkt` file provides identical functionality to the original Clojure implementation while leveraging Racket's syntax and standard library.

## Key Features Implemented

The Racket version includes all core functionality from the original:

- **Recipe tokenization**: Recognizes ingredients, measurements, temperatures, and cooking instructions
- **User preference processing**: Handles system units (metric/imperial), temperature preferences (C/F), portion scaling, and recipe filtering
- **File I/O operations**: Reads recipe files and user option files
- **Pattern matching**: Uses Racket regex to identify complex patterns like fractions (`1/2`, `3/4`), temperatures (`325°F`), and multi-word ingredients
- **Data conversion**: Temperature conversion (F↔C), unit conversions, and portion scaling
- **Parallel processing**: Processes multiple recipe files with chunking support

## Technical Implementation

Key conversions from Clojure to Racket:

```racket
;; Clojure regex patterns converted to Racket
(define rg-temp-f (list "temp-F" #rx"^[0-9]+°F"))
(define rg-nums-frac (list "number-fraction" #rx"^[0-9]+/[0-9]+"))

;; Hash tables for ingredient data
(define ingredient-conversions
  (hash "ingredient-sugar" (hash "cup-to-grams" 200.8634)
        "ingredient-flour" (hash "cup-to-grams" 125.1552)))

;; File reading with Racket's standard library
(define (read-file-lines file-path)
  (if (file-exists? file-path)
      (file->lines file-path)
      '()))
```

## Example Usage

The Racket version processes the same input files and produces equivalent output:

```
$ racket inicio.rkt

-------TOKENIZED
(((r-system system:) (user-cup cup)) 
 ((r-temp temp:) (t-far F)) 
 ((r-portions portions:) (num-portions 6)))

Processing: (recipes/Best Homemade Brownies-1.txt)
Tokenized: ((number-fraction 1/2) (cup cup) (ingredient-sugar granulated sugar))
```

## Testing

The implementation has been tested with:
- User preference files (`options1.txt`, `options2.txt`) 
- Recipe files with complex ingredients and measurements
- Temperature conversion functions
- Fraction parsing and mixed number handling

All core functionality works identically to the original Clojure version while maintaining Racket's functional programming paradigms.
